# gh-1606: Copilot provider: support fine-grained PATs directly (skip exchange, send copilot-developer-cli identity headers) — enables COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN in headless

## Description

## Problem
fa's `copilot` provider only supports one auth path: exchange a GitHub credential via `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token`. That endpoint accepts **only OAuth tokens** (`gho_`/`ghu_` from device flow) — a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`) gets **404** on exchange, and direct Copilot API calls with a raw PAT from a generic HTTP client get **400 "Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint"**. So users who provision a fine-grained PAT (the officially documented token type for Copilot automation) cannot use it in fa at all — while the **official GitHub Copilot CLI can**.

## Evidence (verified empirically, 2026-10-14, Copilot Business seat `copilot_for_business_seat_quota`)
- PAT on exchange: `GET https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` → **404** (any headers/UA, incl. h2, exact CLI UA, `client_id` variants).
- PAT direct on `https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/models` with generic client → **400** `Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint`.
- **PAT + first-party client identity → 200 everywhere.** Adding exactly two headers makes the identical request succeed from plain curl:
  ```
  copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli
  user-agent: copilot/1.0.97 (darwin …) term/unknown
  ```
  - `GET  /models`            → 200 (48 models)
  - `POST /chat/completions`  → 200, real completion (claude-fable-5.1 answered)
- MITM of the official Copilot CLI 1.0.95/1.0.97 with `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=<fine-grained PAT>`: it **never calls the exchange** — it sends the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly to `api.business.githubcopilot.com` with those two headers. Endpoint choice: the exchange's `endpoints.api` for OAuth tokens; for a PAT the CLI picks the seat's endpoint (business/enterprise) directly.
- `ghp_` classic PATs remain unsupported by Copilot at all (unchanged).

## Why it matters for fa
- Headless/docker: a PAT is the ideal credential — stable, revocable, scope-limited, no keychain, no interactive device flow in a container. `export COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` currently **fails** in fa; with this fix it works.
- OAuth device-flow tokens stay the recommended default (they work in both paths); this adds the PAT path.

## Proposed fix
In the copilot provider (`lib/src/providers/copilot_oauth.dart` + key resolution):
1. When the credential is a fine-grained PAT (`isFineGrainedGitHubPat`): **skip the exchange entirely**; use the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly against the Copilot API base URL (config `baseUrl` / provider profile — no `endpoints.api` to learn).
2. Attach the first-party client identity on all Copilot API requests in PAT mode:
   - `copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`
   - `user-agent: copilot/<fa-version> (<os>) term/unknown`
   (These headers are harmless for the OAuth path; decide whether to also send them there for consistency.)
3. Keep the existing exchange flow for `gho_`/`ghu_`/device-flow tokens, including its proactive ~30-min token refresh (unchanged).
4. Update the connect-error hints: for `github_pat_` stop suggesting only the "Copilot Requests" permission edit; explain that PAT mode needs fa ≥ this version or the official CLI.

## Acceptance
1. Unit/integration test (mocked http): credential `github_pat_…` → no request to `copilot_internal/v2/token` is made; requests carry the PAT bearer + the two identity headers; chat completions and models flows work.
2. Live smoke against a Copilot Business seat: `/provider copilot` + pasted fine-grained PAT connects, model list loads, one completion round-trips.
3. OAuth path regression: device-flow token still exchanges, refresh-in-lead behavior preserved (existing tests green).
4. Docs (`docs/` provider page) updated: three supported credentials — device flow (recommended), `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env (OAuth token or fine-grained PAT), classic `ghp_` never supported.

## Notes / honesty
`copilot-developer-cli` is the official CLI's client identity — we present the same first-party integration id the official CLI uses, with the user's own token and seat. GitHub documents fine-grained PATs for the Copilot CLI; using the same identity from a third-party harness is a gray zone users accept knowingly (same pattern as OSS `copilot-api`/`copilot2api` mimicking `vscode-chat`).


## Related UX gap (same card): `/provider export`
There is no fa surface to reveal a stored credential (`/key` is `set|delete` only), so moving the device-flow token to a headless box needs raw `security` incantations. Add one minimal command:

- `/provider export` — copies the full token of the saved Copilot account to the **clipboard**. That's all: no printing to the transcript, no flags, no reveal ceremony. Several accounts → reuse the existing account picker. Feedback is one line: `token copied to clipboard`.

Token-lifetime note (verified): device-flow `gho_`/`ghu_` tokens do not expire and are not refreshed (revocation is manual); only the exchanged ~30-min Copilot API token rotates, which fa re-exchanges automatically — so an exported token stays valid until revoked.

# gh-1606: Copilot provider: support fine-grained PATs directly (skip exchange, send copilot-developer-cli identity headers) — enables COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN in headless

## Description

## Problem
fa's `copilot` provider only supports one auth path: exchange a GitHub credential via `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token`. That endpoint accepts **only OAuth tokens** (`gho_`/`ghu_` from device flow) — a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`) gets **404** on exchange, and direct Copilot API calls with a raw PAT from a generic HTTP client get **400 "Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint"**. So users who provision a fine-grained PAT (the officially documented token type for Copilot automation) cannot use it in fa at all — while the **official GitHub Copilot CLI can**.

## Evidence (verified empirically, 2026-10-14, Copilot Business seat `copilot_for_business_seat_quota`)
- PAT on exchange: `GET https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` → **404** (any headers/UA, incl. h2, exact CLI UA, `client_id` variants).
- PAT direct on `https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/models` with generic client → **400** `Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint`.
- **PAT + first-party client identity → 200 everywhere.** Adding exactly two headers makes the identical request succeed from plain curl:
  ```
  copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli
  user-agent: copilot/1.0.97 (darwin …) term/unknown
  ```
  - `GET  /models`            → 200 (48 models)
  - `POST /chat/completions`  → 200, real completion (claude-fable-5.1 answered)
- MITM of the official Copilot CLI 1.0.95/1.0.97 with `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=<fine-grained PAT>`: it **never calls the exchange** — it sends the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly to `api.business.githubcopilot.com` with those two headers. Endpoint choice: the exchange's `endpoints.api` for OAuth tokens; for a PAT the CLI picks the seat's endpoint (business/enterprise) directly.
- `ghp_` classic PATs remain unsupported by Copilot at all (unchanged).

## Why it matters for fa
- Headless/docker: a PAT is the ideal credential — stable, revocable, scope-limited, no keychain, no interactive device flow in a container. `export COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` currently **fails** in fa; with this fix it works.
- OAuth device-flow tokens stay the recommended default (they work in both paths); this adds the PAT path.

## Proposed fix
In the copilot provider (`lib/src/providers/copilot_oauth.dart` + key resolution):
1. When the credential is a fine-grained PAT (`isFineGrainedGitHubPat`): **skip the exchange entirely**; use the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly against the Copilot API base URL (config `baseUrl` / provider profile — no `endpoints.api` to learn).
2. Attach the first-party client identity on all Copilot API requests in PAT mode:
   - `copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`
   - `user-agent: copilot/<fa-version> (<os>) term/unknown`
   (These headers are harmless for the OAuth path; decide whether to also send them there for consistency.)
3. Keep the existing exchange flow for `gho_`/`ghu_`/device-flow tokens, including its proactive ~30-min token refresh (unchanged).
4. Update the connect-error hints: for `github_pat_` stop suggesting only the "Copilot Requests" permission edit; explain that PAT mode needs fa ≥ this version or the official CLI.

## Acceptance
1. Unit/integration test (mocked http): credential `github_pat_…` → no request to `copilot_internal/v2/token` is made; requests carry the PAT bearer + the two identity headers; chat completions and models flows work.
2. Live smoke against a Copilot Business seat: `/provider copilot` + pasted fine-grained PAT connects, model list loads, one completion round-trips.
3. OAuth path regression: device-flow token still exchanges, refresh-in-lead behavior preserved (existing tests green).
4. Docs (`docs/` provider page) updated: three supported credentials — device flow (recommended), `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env (OAuth token or fine-grained PAT), classic `ghp_` never supported.

## Notes / honesty
`copilot-developer-cli` is the official CLI's client identity — we present the same first-party integration id the official CLI uses, with the user's own token and seat. GitHub documents fine-grained PATs for the Copilot CLI; using the same identity from a third-party harness is a gray zone users accept knowingly (same pattern as OSS `copilot-api`/`copilot2api` mimicking `vscode-chat`).


## Related UX gap (same card): `/provider export`
There is no fa surface to reveal a stored credential (`/key` is `set|delete` only), so moving the device-flow token to a headless box needs raw `security` incantations. Add one minimal command:

- `/provider export` — copies the full token of the saved Copilot account to the **clipboard**. That's all: no printing to the transcript, no flags, no reveal ceremony. Several accounts → reuse the existing account picker. Feedback is one line: `token copied to clipboard`.

Token-lifetime note (verified): device-flow `gho_`/`ghu_` tokens do not expire and are not refreshed (revocation is manual); only the exchanged ~30-min Copilot API token rotates, which fa re-exchanges automatically — so an exported token stays valid until revoked.

blocks.text:
# gh-1606: Copilot provider: support fine-grained PATs directly (skip exchange, send copilot-developer-cli identity headers) — enables COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN in headless

## Description

## Problem
fa's `copilot` provider only supports one auth path: exchange a GitHub credential via `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token`. That endpoint accepts **only OAuth tokens** (`gho_`/`ghu_` from device flow) — a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`) gets **404** on exchange, and direct Copilot API calls with a raw PAT from a generic HTTP client get **400 "Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint"**. So users who provision a fine-grained PAT (the officially documented token type for Copilot automation) cannot use it in fa at all — while the **official GitHub Copilot CLI can**.

## Evidence (verified empirically, 2026-10-14, Copilot Business seat `copilot_for_business_seat_quota`)
- PAT on exchange: `GET https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` → **404** (any headers/UA, incl. h2, exact CLI UA, `client_id` variants).
- PAT direct on `https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/models` with generic client → **400** `Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint`.
- **PAT + first-party client identity → 200 everywhere.** Adding exactly two headers makes the identical request succeed from plain curl:
  ```
  copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli
  user-agent: copilot/1.0.97 (darwin …) term/unknown
  ```
  - `GET  /models`            → 200 (48 models)
  - `POST /chat/completions`  → 200, real completion (claude-fable-5.1 answered)
- MITM of the official Copilot CLI 1.0.95/1.0.97 with `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=<fine-grained PAT>`: it **never calls the exchange** — it sends the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly to `api.business.githubcopilot.com` with those two headers. Endpoint choice: the exchange's `endpoints.api` for OAuth tokens; for a PAT the CLI picks the seat's endpoint (business/enterprise) directly.
- `ghp_` classic PATs remain unsupported by Copilot at all (unchanged).

## Why it matters for fa
- Headless/docker: a PAT is the ideal credential — stable, revocable, scope-limited, no keychain, no interactive device flow in a container. `export COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` currently **fails** in fa; with this fix it works.
- OAuth device-flow tokens stay the recommended default (they work in both paths); this adds the PAT path.

## Proposed fix
In the copilot provider (`lib/src/providers/copilot_oauth.dart` + key resolution):
1. When the credential is a fine-grained PAT (`isFineGrainedGitHubPat`): **skip the exchange entirely**; use the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly against the Copilot API base URL (config `baseUrl` / provider profile — no `endpoints.api` to learn).
2. Attach the first-party client identity on all Copilot API requests in PAT mode:
   - `copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`
   - `user-agent: copilot/<fa-version> (<os>) term/unknown`
   (These headers are harmless for the OAuth path; decide whether to also send them there for consistency.)
3. Keep the existing exchange flow for `gho_`/`ghu_`/device-flow tokens, including its proactive ~30-min token refresh (unchanged).
4. Update the connect-error hints: for `github_pat_` stop suggesting only the "Copilot Requests" permission edit; explain that PAT mode needs fa ≥ this version or the official CLI.

## Acceptance
1. Unit/integration test (mocked http): credential `github_pat_…` → no request to `copilot_internal/v2/token` is made; requests carry the PAT bearer + the two identity headers; chat completions and models flows work.
2. Live smoke against a Copilot Business seat: `/provider copilot` + pasted fine-grained PAT connects, model list loads, one completion round-trips.
3. OAuth path regression: device-flow token still exchanges, refresh-in-lead behavior preserved (existing tests green).
4. Docs (`docs/` provider page) updated: three supported credentials — device flow (recommended), `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env (OAuth token or fine-grained PAT), classic `ghp_` never supported.

## Notes / honesty
`copilot-developer-cli` is the official CLI's client identity — we present the same first-party integration id the official CLI uses, with the user's own token and seat. # gh-1606: Copilot provider: support fine-grained PATs directly (skip exchange, send copilot-developer-cli identity headers) — enables COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN in headless

## Description

## Problem
fa's `copilot` provider only supports one auth path: exchange a GitHub credential via `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token`. That endpoint accepts **only OAuth tokens** (`gho_`/`ghu_` from device flow) — a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`) gets **404** on exchange, and direct Copilot API calls with a raw PAT from a generic HTTP client get **400 "Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint"**. So users who provision a fine-grained PAT (the officially documented token type for Copilot automation) cannot use it in fa at all — while the **official GitHub Copilot CLI can**.

## Evidence (verified empirically, 2026-10-14, Copilot Business seat `copilot_for_business_seat_quota`)
- PAT on exchange: `GET https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` → **404** (any headers/UA, incl. h2, exact CLI UA, `client_id` variants).
- PAT direct on `https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/models` with generic client → **400** `Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint`.
- **PAT + first-party client identity → 200 everywhere.** Adding exactly two headers makes the identical request succeed from plain curl:
  ```
  copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli
  user-agent: copilot/1.0.97 (darwin …) term/unknown
  ```
  - `GET  /models`            → 200 (48 models)
  - `POST /chat/completions`  → 200, real completion (claude-fable-5.1 answered)
- MITM of the official Copilot CLI 1.0.95/1.0.97 with `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=<fine-grained PAT>`: it **never calls the exchange** — it sends the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly to `api.business.githubcopilot.com` with those two headers. Endpoint choice: the exchange's `endpoints.api` for OAuth tokens; for a PAT the CLI picks the seat's endpoint (business/enterprise) directly.
- `ghp_` classic PATs remain unsupported by Copilot at all (unchanged).

## Why it matters for fa
- Headless/docker: a PAT is the ideal credential — stable, revocable, scope-limited, no keychain, no interactive device flow in a container. `export COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` currently **fails** in fa; with this fix it works.
- OAuth device-flow tokens stay the recommended default (they work in both paths); this adds the PAT path.

## Proposed fix
In the copilot provider (`lib/src/providers/copilot_oauth.dart` + key resolution):
1. When the credential is a fine-grained PAT (`isFineGrainedGitHubPat`): **skip the exchange entirely**; use the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly against the Copilot API base URL (config `baseUrl` / provider profile — no `endpoints.api` to learn).
2. Attach the first-party client identity on all Copilot API requests in PAT mode:
   - `copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`
   - `user-agent: copilot/<fa-version> (<os>) term/unknown`
   (These headers are harmless for the OAuth path; decide whether to also send them there for consistency.)
3. Keep the existing exchange flow for `gho_`/`ghu_`/device-flow tokens, including its proactive ~30-min token refresh (unchanged).
4. Update the connect-error hints: for `github_pat_` stop suggesting only the "Copilot Requests" permission edit; explain that PAT mode needs fa ≥ this version or the official CLI.

## Acceptance
1. Unit/integration test (mocked http): credential `github_pat_…` → no request to `copilot_internal/v2/token` is made; requests carry the PAT bearer + the two identity headers; chat completions and models flows work.
2. Live smoke against a Copilot Business seat: `/provider copilot` + pasted fine-grained PAT connects, model list loads, one completion round-trips.
3. OAuth path regression: device-flow token still exchanges, refresh-in-lead behavior preserved (existing tests green).
4. Docs (`docs/` provider page) updated: three supported credentials — device flow (recommended), `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env (OAuth token or fine-grained PAT), classic `ghp_` never supported.

## Notes / honesty
`copilot-developer-cli` is the official CLI's client identity — we present the same first-party integration id the official CLI uses, with the user's own token and seat. GitHub documents fine-grained PATs for the Copilot CLI; using the same identity from a third-party harness is a gray zone users accept knowingly (same pattern as OSS `copilot-api`/`copilot2api` mimicking `vscode-chat`).


## Related UX gap (same card): `/provider export`
There is no fa surface to reveal a stored credential (`/key` is `set|delete` only), so moving the device-flow token to a headless box needs raw `security` incantations. Add one minimal command:

- `/provider export` — copies the full token of the saved Copilot account to the **clipboard**. That's all: no printing to the transcript, no flags, no reveal ceremony. Several accounts → reuse the existing account picker. Feedback is one line: `token copied to clipboard`.

Token-lifetime note (verified): device-flow `gho_`/`ghu_` tokens do not expire and are not refreshed (revocation is manual); only the exchanged ~30-min Copilot API token rotates, which fa re-exchanges automatically — so an exported token stays valid until revoked.

# gh-1606: Copilot provider: support fine-grained PATs directly (skip exchange, send copilot-developer-cli identity headers) — enables COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN in headless

## Description

## Problem
fa's `copilot` provider only supports one auth path: exchange a GitHub credential via `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token`. That endpoint accepts **only OAuth tokens** (`gho_`/`ghu_` from device flow) — a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`) gets **404** on exchange, and direct Copilot API calls with a raw PAT from a generic HTTP client get **400 "Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint"**. So users who provision a fine-grained PAT (the officially documented token type for Copilot automation) cannot use it in fa at all — while the **official GitHub Copilot CLI can**.

## Evidence (verified empirically, 2026-10-14, Copilot Business seat `copilot_for_business_seat_quota`)
- PAT on exchange: `GET https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` → **404** (any headers/UA, incl. h2, exact CLI UA, `client_id` variants).
- PAT direct on `https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/models` with generic client → **400** `Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint`.
- **PAT + first-party client identity → 200 everywhere.** Adding exactly two headers makes the identical request succeed from plain curl:
  ```
  copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli
  user-agent: copilot/1.0.97 (darwin …) term/unknown
  ```
  - `GET  /models`            → 200 (48 models)
  - `POST /chat/completions`  → 200, real completion (claude-fable-5.1 answered)
- MITM of the official Copilot CLI 1.0.95/1.0.97 with `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=<fine-grained PAT>`: it **never calls the exchange** — it sends the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly to `api.business.githubcopilot.com` with those two headers. Endpoint choice: the exchange's `endpoints.api` for OAuth tokens; for a PAT the CLI picks the seat's endpoint (business/enterprise) directly.
- `ghp_` classic PATs remain unsupported by Copilot at all (unchanged).

## Why it matters for fa
- Headless/docker: a PAT is the ideal credential — stable, revocable, scope-limited, no keychain, no interactive device flow in a container. `export COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` currently **fails** in fa; with this fix it works.
- OAuth device-flow tokens stay the recommended default (they work in both paths); this adds the PAT path.

## Proposed fix
In the copilot provider (`lib/src/providers/copilot_oauth.dart` + key resolution):
1. When the credential is a fine-grained PAT (`isFineGrainedGitHubPat`): **skip the exchange entirely**; use the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly against the Copilot API base URL (config `baseUrl` / provider profile — no `endpoints.api` to learn).
2. Attach the first-party client identity on all Copilot API requests in PAT mode:
   - `copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`
   - `user-agent: copilot/<fa-version> (<os>) term/unknown`
   (These headers are harmless for the OAuth path; decide whether to also send them there for consistency.)
3. Keep the existing exchange flow for `gho_`/`ghu_`/device-flow tokens, including its proactive ~30-min token refresh (unchanged).
4. Update the connect-error hints: for `github_pat_` stop suggesting only the "Copilot Requests" permission edit; explain that PAT mode needs fa ≥ this version or the official CLI.

## Acceptance
1. Unit/integration test (mocked http): credential `github_pat_…` → no request to `copilot_internal/v2/token` is made; requests carry the PAT bearer + the two identity headers; chat completions and models flows work.
2. Live smoke against a Copilot Business seat: `/provider copilot` + pasted fine-grained PAT connects, model list loads, one completion round-trips.
3. OAuth path regression: device-flow token still exchanges, refresh-in-lead behavior preserved (existing tests green).
4. Docs (`docs/` provider page) updated: three supported credentials — device flow (recommended), `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env (OAuth token or fine-grained PAT), classic `ghp_` never supported.

## Notes / honesty
`copilot-developer-cli` is the official CLI's client identity — we present the same first-party integration id the official CLI uses, with the user's own token and seat. GitHub documents fine-grained PATs for the Copilot CLI; using the same identity from a third-party harness is a gray zone users accept knowingly (same pattern as OSS `copilot-api`/`copilot2api` mimicking `vscode-chat`).


## Related UX gap (same card): `/provider export`
There is no fa surface to reveal a stored credential (`/key` is `set|delete` only), so moving the device-flow token to a headless box needs raw `security` incantations. Add one minimal command:

- `/provider export` — copies the full token of the saved Copilot account to the **clipboard**. That's all: no printing to the transcript, no flags, no reveal ceremony. Several accounts → reuse the existing account picker. Feedback is one line: `token copied to clipboard`.

Token-lifetime note (verified): device-flow `gho_`/`ghu_` tokens do not expire and are not refreshed (revocation is manual); only the exchanged ~30-min Copilot API token rotates, which fa re-exchanges automatically — so an exported token stays valid until revoked.

Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] CI -->|No| THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for PR Rework — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start from the concrete issue: a CI failure, a review thread, or a BLOCKING/IMPORTANT finding"] T1["RED: Write or extend a test that REPRODUCES the reported issue
— must fail before the fix
— cover the exact scenario called out (including boundary/multi-item cases, not just the happy path)"] T2["GREEN: Make the minimum code change to turn the test PASS
— do not expand scope beyond the reported issue"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— run the full test suite after every change"] T4{"More findings to address?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for the next finding"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 T4 -->|No| DONE([All findings fixed with regression tests]) end subgraph RULES["PR Rework TDD Rules"] R1["❌ NEVER change production code in response to a review comment or CI failure without a test that first reproduces it"] R2["✅ If the existing tests only cover a single-item/simple case, add a test for the multi-item/edge case the finding points at — a fix without a test for that exact case is not verified"] R3["✅ Returned findings: your fix must differ from the previous attempt and the new/updated test must prove it"] R4["✅ Run the FULL test suite before finishing — no regressions allowed"] R5["✅ Verification order: finalize ALL fixes BEFORE launching the full test-suite/coverage run — a run over a tree you are still editing is wasted"] R6["✅ Long runs (full suite, coverage) start with bash background: true and are collected via bash_job status/output between other steps — NEVER foreground sleep-polling (see prompts/bash_tools.md)"] R7["❌ NEVER kill a running verification because files changed after it started — let it finish, treat the result as stale, re-run deliberately"] end TDD --> RULES ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD F1["outputs/response.md must be Markdown (# headings, - bullets, ``` code fences)"] F2["Required sections: ## Issues/Notes (if any), ## Approach, ## Files Modified, ## Test Coverage"] F3["Be surgical but thorough — fix exact issues flagged, then check same pattern across codebase"] F4["Do NOT refactor unrelated code or add unrequested features"] F5["When open PR review threads exist, create outputs/review_replies/*.md files and reference them from outputs/review_replies.json"] ``` - When `input//pr_discussions_raw.json` contains open PR review threads: - Write one Markdown file per open thread under `outputs/review_replies/`. - Write `outputs/review_replies.json` with one entry per open thread, including `inReplyToId`, `threadId`, and a `reply` field that contains the path to the matching `.md` file. - Do **not** put reply bodies inline in the JSON. ## PR Rework — Output Rules Rework posts **only** to the Pull Request. # gh-1606: Copilot provider: support fine-grained PATs directly (skip exchange, send copilot-developer-cli identity headers) — enables COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN in headless

## Description

## Problem
fa's `copilot` provider only supports one auth path: exchange a GitHub credential via `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token`. That endpoint accepts **only OAuth tokens** (`gho_`/`ghu_` from device flow) — a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`) gets **404** on exchange, and direct Copilot API calls with a raw PAT from a generic HTTP client get **400 "Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint"**. So users who provision a fine-grained PAT (the officially documented token type for Copilot automation) cannot use it in fa at all — while the **official GitHub Copilot CLI can**.

## Evidence (verified empirically, 2026-10-14, Copilot Business seat `copilot_for_business_seat_quota`)
- PAT on exchange: `GET https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` → **404** (any headers/UA, incl. h2, exact CLI UA, `client_id` variants).
- PAT direct on `https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/models` with generic client → **400** `Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint`.
- **PAT + first-party client identity → 200 everywhere.** Adding exactly two headers makes the identical request succeed from plain curl:
  ```
  copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli
  user-agent: copilot/1.0.97 (darwin …) term/unknown
  ```
  - `GET  /models`            → 200 (48 models)
  - `POST /chat/completions`  → 200, real completion (claude-fable-5.1 answered)
- MITM of the official Copilot CLI 1.0.95/1.0.97 with `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=<fine-grained PAT>`: it **never calls the exchange** — it sends the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly to `api.business.githubcopilot.com` with those two headers. Endpoint choice: the exchange's `endpoints.api` for OAuth tokens; for a PAT the CLI picks the seat's endpoint (business/enterprise) directly.
- `ghp_` classic PATs remain unsupported by Copilot at all (unchanged).

## Why it matters for fa
- Headless/docker: a PAT is the ideal credential — stable, revocable, scope-limited, no keychain, no interactive device flow in a container. `export COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` currently **fails** in fa; with this fix it works.
- OAuth device-flow tokens stay the recommended default (they work in both paths); this adds the PAT path.

## Proposed fix
In the copilot provider (`lib/src/providers/copilot_oauth.dart` + key resolution):
1. When the credential is a fine-grained PAT (`isFineGrainedGitHubPat`): **skip the exchange entirely**; use the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly against the Copilot API base URL (config `baseUrl` / provider profile — no `endpoints.api` to learn).
2. Attach the first-party client identity on all Copilot API requests in PAT mode:
   - `copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`
   - `user-agent: copilot/<fa-version> (<os>) term/unknown`
   (These headers are harmless for the OAuth path; decide whether to also send them there for consistency.)
3. Keep the existing exchange flow for `gho_`/`ghu_`/device-flow tokens, including its proactive ~30-min token refresh (unchanged).
4. Update the connect-error hints: for `github_pat_` stop suggesting only the "Copilot Requests" permission edit; explain that PAT mode needs fa ≥ this version or the official CLI.

## Acceptance
1. Unit/integration test (mocked http): credential `github_pat_…` → no request to `copilot_internal/v2/token` is made; requests carry the PAT bearer + the two identity headers; chat completions and models flows work.
2. Live smoke against a Copilot Business seat: `/provider copilot` + pasted fine-grained PAT connects, model list loads, one completion round-trips.
3. OAuth path regression: device-flow token still exchanges, refresh-in-lead behavior preserved (existing tests green).
4. Docs (`docs/` provider page) updated: three supported credentials — device flow (recommended), `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env (OAuth token or fine-grained PAT), classic `ghp_` never supported.

## Notes / honesty
`copilot-developer-cli` is the official CLI's client identity — we present the same first-party integration id the official CLI uses, with the user's own token and seat. GitHub documents fine-grained PATs for the Copilot CLI; using the same identity from a third-party harness is a gray zone users accept knowingly (same pattern as OSS `copilot-api`/`copilot2api` mimicking `vscode-chat`).


## Related UX gap (same card): `/provider export`
There is no fa surface to reveal a stored credential (`/key` is `set|delete` only), so moving the device-flow token to a headless box needs raw `security` incantations. Add one minimal command:

- `/provider export` — copies the full token of the saved Copilot account to the **clipboard**. That's all: no printing to the transcript, no flags, no reveal ceremony. Several accounts → reuse the existing account picker. Feedback is one line: `token copied to clipboard`.

Token-lifetime note (verified): device-flow `gho_`/`ghu_` tokens do not expire and are not refreshed (revocation is manual); only the exchanged ~30-min Copilot API token rotates, which fa re-exchanges automatically — so an exported token stays valid until revoked.

# gh-1606: Copilot provider: support fine-grained PATs directly (skip exchange, send copilot-developer-cli identity headers) — enables COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN in headless

## Description

## Problem
fa's `copilot` provider only supports one auth path: exchange a GitHub credential via `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token`. That endpoint accepts **only OAuth tokens** (`gho_`/`ghu_` from device flow) — a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`) gets **404** on exchange, and direct Copilot API calls with a raw PAT from a generic HTTP client get **400 "Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint"**. So users who provision a fine-grained PAT (the officially documented token type for Copilot automation) cannot use it in fa at all — while the **official GitHub Copilot CLI can**.

## Evidence (verified empirically, 2026-10-14, Copilot Business seat `copilot_for_business_seat_quota`)
- PAT on exchange: `GET https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` → **404** (any headers/UA, incl. h2, exact CLI UA, `client_id` variants).
- PAT direct on `https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/models` with generic client → **400** `Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint`.
- **PAT + first-party client identity → 200 everywhere.** Adding exactly two headers makes the identical request succeed from plain curl:
  ```
  copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli
  user-agent: copilot/1.0.97 (darwin …) term/unknown
  ```
  - `GET  /models`            → 200 (48 models)
  - `POST /chat/completions`  → 200, real completion (claude-fable-5.1 answered)
- MITM of the official Copilot CLI 1.0.95/1.0.97 with `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=<fine-grained PAT>`: it **never calls the exchange** — it sends the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly to `api.business.githubcopilot.com` with those two headers. Endpoint choice: the exchange's `endpoints.api` for OAuth tokens; for a PAT the CLI picks the seat's endpoint (business/enterprise) directly.
- `ghp_` classic PATs remain unsupported by Copilot at all (unchanged).

## Why it matters for fa
- Headless/docker: a PAT is the ideal credential — stable, revocable, scope-limited, no keychain, no interactive device flow in a container. `export COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` currently **fails** in fa; with this fix it works.
- OAuth device-flow tokens stay the recommended default (they work in both paths); this adds the PAT path.

## Proposed fix
In the copilot provider (`lib/src/providers/copilot_oauth.dart` + key resolution):
1. When the credential is a fine-grained PAT (`isFineGrainedGitHubPat`): **skip the exchange entirely**; use the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly against the Copilot API base URL (config `baseUrl` / provider profile — no `endpoints.api` to learn).
2. Attach the first-party client identity on all Copilot API requests in PAT mode:
   - `copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`
   - `user-agent: copilot/<fa-version> (<os>) term/unknown`
   (These headers are harmless for the OAuth path; decide whether to also send them there for consistency.)
3. Keep the existing exchange flow for `gho_`/`ghu_`/device-flow tokens, including its proactive ~30-min token refresh (unchanged).
4. Update the connect-error hints: for `github_pat_` stop suggesting only the "Copilot Requests" permission edit; explain that PAT mode needs fa ≥ this version or the official CLI.

## Acceptance
1. Unit/integration test (mocked http): credential `github_pat_…` → no request to `copilot_internal/v2/token` is made; requests carry the PAT bearer + the two identity headers; chat completions and models flows work.
2. Live smoke against a Copilot Business seat: `/provider copilot` + pasted fine-grained PAT connects, model list loads, one completion round-trips.
3. OAuth path regression: device-flow token still exchanges, refresh-in-lead behavior preserved (existing tests green).
4. Docs (`docs/` provider page) updated: three supported credentials — device flow (recommended), `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env (OAuth token or fine-grained PAT), classic `ghp_` never supported.

## Notes / honesty
`copilot-developer-cli` is the official CLI's client identity — we present the same first-party integration id the official CLI uses, with the user's own token and seat. GitHub documents fine-grained PATs for the Copilot CLI; using the same identity from a third-party harness is a gray zone users accept knowingly (same pattern as OSS `copilot-api`/`copilot2api` mimicking `vscode-chat`).


## Related UX gap (same card): `/provider export`
There is no fa surface to reveal a stored credential (`/key` is `set|delete` only), so moving the device-flow token to a headless box needs raw `security` incantations. Add one minimal command:

- `/provider export` — copies the full token of the saved Copilot account to the **clipboard**. That's all: no printing to the transcript, no flags, no reveal ceremony. Several accounts → reuse the existing account picker. Feedback is one line: `token copied to clipboard`.

Token-lifetime note (verified): device-flow `gho_`/`ghu_` tokens do not expire and are not refreshed (revocation is manual); only the exchanged ~30-min Copilot API token rotates, which fa re-exchanges automatically — so an exported token stays valid until revoked.

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add bullets, ``` code fences)"] F2["Required sections: ## Issues/Notes (if any), ## Approach, ## Files Modified, ## Test Coverage"] F3["Be surgical but thorough — fix exact issues flagged, then check same pattern across codebase"] F4["Do NOT refactor unrelated code or add unrequested features"] F5["When open PR review threads exist, create outputs/review_replies/*.md files and reference them from outputs/review_replies.json"] ``` - This is the only request shape the Copilot API accepts a PAT with; `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` now works headless. - New `/provider export`: copies the saved Copilot account's full token to the clipboard (single account = no ceremony; several = the existing account picker; feedback is one line `token copied to clipboard`; the token never prints to the transcript). - Connect flow updated: the PAT paste hint explains direct-PAT mode (device flow stays recommended); a dead PAT surfaces at the model fetch ("no models for this PAT — check Copilot Requests permission/seat") instead of a forecast exchange 404. ### Key decisions - **PAT mode lives in the token source**: `CopilotTokenManager.get()` short-circuits PATs (no exchange, no cache, no refresh); `copilotRequestHeaders()` dispatches request headers by token shape — an exchanged token keeps the `vscode-chat` identity byte-for-byte, a PAT presents `copilot-developer-cli`. The 401/403 refresh-retry is skipped in PAT mode (nothing to refresh — no doomed retry). - The `/models` dialect gets the same split: PAT → `GET {configured-base}/models` with PAT headers; OAuth → existing exchange + `proxy-ep` derivation, untouched. - Version/OS for the user-agent are host-installed at startup (`installCopilotCliIdentity` in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`) — `lib/` stays pure Dart. - Clipboard writes go through a new `clipboard_writer.dart` (pbcopy / xclip→wl-copy / clip; the token rides **stdin**, never argv) behind the same web-safe conditional-import pattern as the pasteboard reader, plus an `AgentCliConfig.clipboardWrite` test seam. - OAuth path unchanged: exchange, proactive ~30-min refresh, 401 refresh+retry all preserved (existing tests green). ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/copilot_test.dart # PAT mode group: no exchange, PAT bearer + identity headers, chat + /models dart test test/cli/copilot_provider_test.dart test/cli/clipboard_writer_test.dart ``` Docs: `docs/agents/providers.md` (new "GitHub Copilot credentials" table — device flow recommended / `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env as OAuth or fine-grained PAT / classic `ghp_` never supported), README Copilot section, CHANGELOG under Unreleased. **Not verified here**: the live smoke against a real Copilot Business seat (AC2) — this ephemeral CI runner holds no Copilot-seat credential; AC1's mocked-http tests cover the wire shape the smoke would check.

blocks.text:
# gh-1606: Copilot provider: support fine-grained PATs directly (skip exchange, send copilot-developer-cli identity headers) — enables COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN in headless

## Description

## Problem
fa's `copilot` provider only supports one auth path: exchange a GitHub credential via `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token`. That endpoint accepts **only OAuth tokens** (`gho_`/`ghu_` from device flow) — a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`) gets **404** on exchange, and direct Copilot API calls with a raw PAT from a generic HTTP client get **400 "Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint"**. So users who provision a fine-grained PAT (the officially documented token type for Copilot automation) cannot use it in fa at all — while the **official GitHub Copilot CLI can**.

## Evidence (verified empirically, 2026-10-14, Copilot Business seat `copilot_for_business_seat_quota`)
- PAT on exchange: `GET https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` → **404** (any headers/UA, incl. h2, exact CLI UA, `client_id` variants).
- PAT direct on `https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/models` with generic client → **400** `Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint`.
- **PAT + first-party client identity → 200 everywhere.** Adding exactly two headers makes the identical request succeed from plain curl:
  ```
  copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli
  user-agent: copilot/1.0.97 (darwin …) term/unknown
  ```
  - `GET  /models`            → 200 (48 models)
  - `POST /chat/completions`  → 200, real completion (claude-fable-5.1 answered)
- MITM of the official Copilot CLI 1.0.95/1.0.97 with `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=<fine-grained PAT>`: it **never calls the exchange** — it sends the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly to `api.business.githubcopilot.com` with those two headers. Endpoint choice: the exchange's `endpoints.api` for OAuth tokens; for a PAT the CLI picks the seat's endpoint (business/enterprise) directly.
- `ghp_` classic PATs remain unsupported by Copilot at all (unchanged).

## Why it matters for fa
- Headless/docker: a PAT is the ideal credential — stable, revocable, scope-limited, no keychain, no interactive device flow in a container. `export COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` currently **fails** in fa; with this fix it works.
- OAuth device-flow tokens stay the recommended default (they work in both paths); this adds the PAT path.

## Proposed fix
In the copilot provider (`lib/src/providers/copilot_oauth.dart` + key resolution):
1. When the credential is a fine-grained PAT (`isFineGrainedGitHubPat`): **skip the exchange entirely**; use the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly against the Copilot API base URL (config `baseUrl` / provider profile — no `endpoints.api` to learn).
2. Attach the first-party client identity on all Copilot API requests in PAT mode:
   - `copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`
   - `user-agent: copilot/<fa-version> (<os>) term/unknown`
   (These headers are harmless for the OAuth path; decide whether to also send them there for consistency.)
3. Keep the existing exchange flow for `gho_`/`ghu_`/device-flow tokens, including its proactive ~30-min token refresh (unchanged).
4. Update the connect-error hints: for `github_pat_` stop suggesting only the "Copilot Requests" permission edit; explain that PAT mode needs fa ≥ this version or the official CLI.

## Acceptance
1. Unit/integration test (mocked http): credential `github_pat_…` → no request to `copilot_internal/v2/token` is made; requests carry the PAT bearer + the two identity headers; chat completions and models flows work.
2. Live smoke against a Copilot Business seat: `/provider copilot` + pasted fine-grained PAT connects, model list loads, one completion round-trips.
3. OAuth path regression: device-flow token still exchanges, refresh-in-lead behavior preserved (existing tests green).
4. Docs (`docs/` provider page) updated: three supported credentials — device flow (recommended), `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env (OAuth token or fine-grained PAT), classic `ghp_` never supported.

## Notes / honesty
`copilot-developer-cli` is the official CLI's client identity — we present the same first-party integration id the official CLI uses, with the user's own token and seat. GitHub documents fine-grained PATs for the Copilot CLI; using the same identity from a third-party harness is a gray zone users accept knowingly (same pattern as OSS `copilot-api`/`copilot2api` mimicking `vscode-chat`).


## Related UX gap (same card): `/provider export`
There is no fa surface to reveal a stored credential (`/key` is `set|delete` only), so moving the device-flow token to a headless box needs raw `security` incantations. Add one minimal command:

- `/provider export` — copies the full token of the saved Copilot account to the **clipboard**. That's all: no printing to the transcript, no flags, no reveal ceremony. Several accounts → reuse the existing account picker. Feedback is one line: `token copied to clipboard`.

Token-lifetime note (verified): device-flow `gho_`/`ghu_` tokens do not expire and are not refreshed (revocation is manual); only the exchanged ~30-min Copilot API token rotates, which fa re-exchanges automatically — so an exported token stays valid until revoked.

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1608 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1608 - **Title**: gh-1606 Copilot provider: support fine-grained PATs directly (skip exchange, send copilot-developer-cli identity headers) — enables COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN in headless - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1606` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 19 - **Additions**: +1042 - **Deletions**: -60 - **Created**: 2026-10-14T12:30:53Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-14T12:51:26Z ## PR Description Closes #1606 # gh-1606 — Copilot provider: fine-grained PAT support (PAT mode) + `/provider export` ### What changed - The `copilot` provider now accepts fine-grained PATs (`github_pat_…`) **directly**: when the GitHub credential is a PAT, the `copilot_internal/v2/token` exchange is skipped entirely and the raw PAT rides as the Bearer against the configured Copilot base URL (the seat's tier host — a PAT has no `proxy-ep` to learn a tenant host from), with the official Copilot CLI's first-party identity headers (`copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`, `user-agent: copilot/ () term/unknown`). This is the only request shape the Copilot API accepts a PAT with; `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` now works headless. - New `/provider export`: copies the saved Copilot account's full token to the clipboard (single account = no ceremony; several = the existing account picker; feedback is one line `token copied to clipboard`; the token never prints to the transcript). - Connect flow updated: the PAT paste hint explains direct-PAT mode (device flow stays recommended); a dead PAT surfaces at the model fetch ("no models for this PAT — check Copilot Requests permission/seat") instead of a forecast exchange 404. ### Key decisions - **PAT mode lives in the token source**: `CopilotTokenManager.get()` short-circuits PATs (no exchange, no cache, no refresh); `copilotRequestHeaders()` dispatches request headers by token shape — an exchanged token keeps the `vscode-chat` identity byte-for-byte, a PAT presents `copilot-developer-cli`. The 401/403 refresh-retry is skipped in PAT mode (nothing to refresh — no doomed retry). - The `/models` dialect gets the same split: PAT → `GET {configured-base}/models` with PAT headers; OAuth → existing exchange + `proxy-ep` derivation, untouched. - Version/OS for the user-agent are host-installed at startup (`installCopilotCliIdentity` in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`) — `lib/` stays pure Dart. - Clipboard writes go through a new `clipboard_writer.dart` (pbcopy / xclip→wl-copy / clip; the token rides **stdin**, never argv) behind the same web-safe conditional-import pattern as the pasteboard reader, plus an `AgentCliConfig.clipboardWrite` test seam. - OAuth path unchanged: exchange, proactive ~30-min refresh, 401 refresh+retry all preserved (existing tests green). ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/copilot_test.dart # PAT mode group: no exchange, PAT bearer + identity headers, chat + /models dart test test/cli/copilot_provider_test.dart test/cli/clipboard_writer_test.dart ``` Docs: `docs/agents/providers.md` (new "GitHub Copilot credentials" table — device flow recommended / `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env as OAuth or fine-grained PAT / classic `ghp_` never supported), README Copilot section, CHANGELOG under Unreleased. **Not verified here**: the live smoke against a real Copilot Business seat (AC2) — this ephemeral CI runner holds no Copilot-seat credential; AC1's mocked-http tests cover the wire shape the smoke would check.
Request flow ```mermaid flowchart TD CRED[GitHub credential] -->|gho_/ghu_ OAuth| EX[POST copilot_internal/v2/token exchange] EX --> TOK[~30-min Copilot API token + proxy-ep host] CRED -->|github_pat_ PAT| PAT[raw PAT is the Bearer] TOK --> API[copilot API base URL] PAT --> API API --> HDR[vscode-chat identity · OAuth
copilot-developer-cli + copilot/<version> UA · PAT] HDR --> MODELS[GET /models] HDR --> CHAT[POST /chat/completions] ```

blocks.text:
# gh-1606: Copilot provider: support fine-grained PATs directly (skip exchange, send copilot-developer-cli identity headers) — enables COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN in headless

## Description

## Problem
fa's `copilot` provider only supports one auth path: exchange a GitHub credential via `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token`. That endpoint accepts **only OAuth tokens** (`gho_`/`ghu_` from device flow) — a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`) gets **404** on exchange, and direct Copilot API calls with a raw PAT from a generic HTTP client get **400 "Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint"**. So users who provision a fine-grained PAT (the officially documented token type for Copilot automation) cannot use it in fa at all — while the **official GitHub Copilot CLI can**.

## Evidence (verified empirically, 2026-10-14, Copilot Business seat `copilot_for_business_seat_quota`)
- PAT on exchange: `GET https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` → **404** (any headers/UA, incl. h2, exact CLI UA, `client_id` variants).
- PAT direct on `https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/models` with generic client → **400** `Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint`.
- **PAT + first-party client identity → 200 everywhere.** Adding exactly two headers makes the identical request succeed from plain curl:
  ```
  copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli
  user-agent: copilot/1.0.97 (darwin …) term/unknown
  ```
  - `GET  /models`            → 200 (48 models)
  - `POST /chat/completions`  → 200, real completion (claude-fable-5.1 answered)
- MITM of the official Copilot CLI 1.0.95/1.0.97 with `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=<fine-grained PAT>`: it **never calls the exchange** — it sends the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly to `api.business.githubcopilot.com` with those two headers. Endpoint choice: the exchange's `endpoints.api` for OAuth tokens; for a PAT the CLI picks the seat's endpoint (business/enterprise) directly.
- `ghp_` classic PATs remain unsupported by Copilot at all (unchanged).

## Why it matters for fa
- Headless/docker: a PAT is the ideal credential — stable, revocable, scope-limited, no keychain, no interactive device flow in a container. `export COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` currently **fails** in fa; with this fix it works.
- OAuth device-flow tokens stay the recommended default (they work in both paths); this adds the PAT path.

## Proposed fix
In the copilot provider (`lib/src/providers/copilot_oauth.dart` + key resolution):
1. When the credential is a fine-grained PAT (`isFineGrainedGitHubPat`): **skip the exchange entirely**; use the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly against the Copilot API base URL (config `baseUrl` / provider profile — no `endpoints.api` to learn).
2. Attach the first-party client identity on all Copilot API requests in PAT mode:
   - `copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`
   - `user-agent: copilot/<fa-version> (<os>) term/unknown`
   (These headers are harmless for the OAuth path; decide whether to also send them there for consistency.)
3. Keep the existing exchange flow for `gho_`/`ghu_`/device-flow tokens, including its proactive ~30-min token refresh (unchanged).
4. Update the connect-error hints: for `github_pat_` stop suggesting only the "Copilot Requests" permission edit; explain that PAT mode needs fa ≥ this version or the official CLI.

## Acceptance
1. Unit/integration test (mocked http): credential `github_pat_…` → no request to `copilot_internal/v2/token` is made; requests carry the PAT bearer + the two identity headers; chat completions and models flows work.
2. Live smoke against a Copilot Business seat: `/provider copilot` + pasted fine-grained PAT connects, model list loads, one completion round-trips.
3. OAuth path regression: device-flow token still exchanges, refresh-in-lead behavior preserved (existing tests green).
4. Docs (`docs/` provider page) updated: three supported credentials — device flow (recommended), `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env (OAuth token or fine-grained PAT), classic `ghp_` never supported.

## Notes / honesty
`copilot-developer-cli` is the official CLI's client identity — we present the same first-party integration id the official CLI uses, with the user's own token and seat. GitHub documents fine-grained PATs for the Copilot CLI; using the same identity from a third-party harness is a gray zone users accept knowingly (same pattern as OSS `copilot-api`/`copilot2api` mimicking `vscode-chat`).


## Related UX gap (same card): `/provider export`
There is no fa surface to reveal a stored credential (`/key` is `set|delete` only), so moving the device-flow token to a headless box needs raw `security` incantations. Add one minimal command:

- `/provider export` — copies the full token of the saved Copilot account to the **clipboard**. That's all: no printing to the transcript, no flags, no reveal ceremony. Several accounts → reuse the existing account picker. Feedback is one line: `token copied to clipboard`.

Token-lifetime note (verified): device-flow `gho_`/`ghu_` tokens do not expire and are not refreshed (revocation is manual); only the exchanged ~30-min Copilot API token rotates, which fa re-exchanges automatically — so an exported token stays valid until revoked.

# gh-1606: Copilot provider: support fine-grained PATs directly (skip exchange, send copilot-developer-cli identity headers) — enables COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN in headless

## Description

## Problem
fa's `copilot` provider only supports one auth path: exchange a GitHub credential via `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token`. That endpoint accepts **only OAuth tokens** (`gho_`/`ghu_` from device flow) — a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`) gets **404** on exchange, and direct Copilot API calls with a raw PAT from a generic HTTP client get **400 "Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint"**. So users who provision a fine-grained PAT (the officially documented token type for Copilot automation) cannot use it in fa at all — while the **official GitHub Copilot CLI can**.

## Evidence (verified empirically, 2026-10-14, Copilot Business seat `copilot_for_business_seat_quota`)
- PAT on exchange: `GET https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` → **404** (any headers/UA, incl. h2, exact CLI UA, `client_id` variants).
- PAT direct on `https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/models` with generic client → **400** `Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint`.
- **PAT + first-party client identity → 200 everywhere.** Adding exactly two headers makes the identical request succeed from plain curl:
  ```
  copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli
  user-agent: copilot/1.0.97 (darwin …) term/unknown
  ```
  - `GET  /models`            → 200 (48 models)
  - `POST /chat/completions`  → 200, real completion (claude-fable-5.1 answered)
- MITM of the official Copilot CLI 1.0.95/1.0.97 with `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=<fine-grained PAT>`: it **never calls the exchange** — it sends the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly to `api.business.githubcopilot.com` with those two headers. Endpoint choice: the exchange's `endpoints.api` for OAuth tokens; for a PAT the CLI picks the seat's endpoint (business/enterprise) directly.
- `ghp_` classic PATs remain unsupported by Copilot at all (unchanged).

## Why it matters for fa
- Headless/docker: a PAT is the ideal credential — stable, revocable, scope-limited, no keychain, no interactive device flow in a container. `export COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` currently **fails** in fa; with this fix it works.
- OAuth device-flow tokens stay the recommended default (they work in both paths); this adds the PAT path.

## Proposed fix
In the copilot provider (`lib/src/providers/copilot_oauth.dart` + key resolution):
1. When the credential is a fine-grained PAT (`isFineGrainedGitHubPat`): **skip the exchange entirely**; use the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly against the Copilot API base URL (config `baseUrl` / provider profile — no `endpoints.api` to learn).
2. Attach the first-party client identity on all Copilot API requests in PAT mode:
   - `copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`
   - `user-agent: copilot/<fa-version> (<os>) term/unknown`
   (These headers are harmless for the OAuth path; decide whether to also send them there for consistency.)
3. Keep the existing exchange flow for `gho_`/`ghu_`/device-flow tokens, including its proactive ~30-min token refresh (unchanged).
4. Update the connect-error hints: for `github_pat_` stop suggesting only the "Copilot Requests" permission edit; explain that PAT mode needs fa ≥ this version or the official CLI.

## Acceptance
1. Unit/integration test (mocked http): credential `github_pat_…` → no request to `copilot_internal/v2/token` is made; requests carry the PAT bearer + the two identity headers; chat completions and models flows work.
2. Live smoke against a Copilot Business seat: `/provider copilot` + pasted fine-grained PAT connects, model list loads, one completion round-trips.
3. OAuth path regression: device-flow token still exchanges, refresh-in-lead behavior preserved (existing tests green).
4. Docs (`docs/` provider page) updated: three supported credentials — device flow (recommended), `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env (OAuth token or fine-grained PAT), classic `ghp_` never supported.

## Notes / honesty
`copilot-developer-cli` is the official CLI's client identity — we present the same first-party integration id the official CLI uses, with the user's own token and seat. GitHub documents fine-grained PATs for the Copilot CLI; using the same identity from a third-party harness is a gray zone users accept knowingly (same pattern as OSS `copilot-api`/`copilot2api` mimicking `vscode-chat`).


## Related UX gap (same card): `/provider export`
There is no fa surface to reveal a stored credential (`/key` is `set|delete` only), so moving the device-flow token to a headless box needs raw `security` incantations. Add one minimal command:

- `/provider export` — copies the full token of the saved Copilot account to the **clipboard**. That's all: no printing to the transcript, no flags, no reveal ceremony. Several accounts → reuse the existing account picker. Feedback is one line: `token copied to clipboard`.

Token-lifetime note (verified): device-flow `gho_`/`ghu_` tokens do not expire and are not refreshed (revocation is manual); only the exchanged ~30-min Copilot API token rotates, which fa re-exchanges automatically — so an exported token stays valid until revoked.

# gh-1606: Copilot provider: support fine-grained PATs directly (skip exchange, send copilot-developer-cli identity headers) — enables COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN in headless

## Description

## Problem
fa's `copilot` provider only supports one auth path: exchange a GitHub credential via `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token`. That endpoint accepts **only OAuth tokens** (`gho_`/`ghu_` from device flow) — a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`) gets **404** on exchange, and direct Copilot API calls with a raw PAT from a generic HTTP client get **400 "Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint"**. So users who provision a fine-grained PAT (the officially documented token type for Copilot automation) cannot use it in fa at all — while the **official GitHub Copilot CLI can**.

## Evidence (verified empirically, 2026-10-14, Copilot Business seat `copilot_for_business_seat_quota`)
- PAT on exchange: `GET https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` → **404** (any headers/UA, incl. h2, exact CLI UA, `client_id` variants).
- PAT direct on `https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/models` with generic client → **400** `Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint`.
- **PAT + first-party client identity → 200 everywhere.** Adding exactly two headers makes the identical request succeed from plain curl:
  ```
  copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli
  user-agent: copilot/1.0.97 (darwin …) term/unknown
  ```
  - `GET  /models`            → 200 (48 models)
  - `POST /chat/completions`  → 200, real completion (claude-fable-5.1 answered)
- MITM of the official Copilot CLI 1.0.95/1.0.97 with `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=<fine-grained PAT>`: it **never calls the exchange** — it sends the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly to `api.business.githubcopilot.com` with those two headers. Endpoint choice: the exchange's `endpoints.api` for OAuth tokens; for a PAT the CLI picks the seat's endpoint (business/enterprise) directly.
- `ghp_` classic PATs remain unsupported by Copilot at all (unchanged).

## Why it matters for fa
- Headless/docker: a PAT is the ideal credential — stable, revocable, scope-limited, no keychain, no interactive device flow in a container. `export COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` currently **fails** in fa; with this fix it works.
- OAuth device-flow tokens stay the recommended default (they work in both paths); this adds the PAT path.

## Proposed fix
In the copilot provider (`lib/src/providers/copilot_oauth.dart` + key resolution):
1. When the credential is a fine-grained PAT (`isFineGrainedGitHubPat`): **skip the exchange entirely**; use the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly against the Copilot API base URL (config `baseUrl` / provider profile — no `endpoints.api` to learn).
2. Attach the first-party client identity on all Copilot API requests in PAT mode:
   - `copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`
   - `user-agent: copilot/<fa-version> (<os>) term/unknown`
   (These headers are harmless for the OAuth path; decide whether to also send them there for consistency.)
3. Keep the existing exchange flow for `gho_`/`ghu_`/device-flow tokens, including its proactive ~30-min token refresh (unchanged).
4. Update the connect-error hints: for `github_pat_` stop suggesting only the "Copilot Requests" permission edit; explain that PAT mode needs fa ≥ this version or the official CLI.

## Acceptance
1. Unit/integration test (mocked http): credential `github_pat_…` → no request to `copilot_internal/v2/token` is made; requests carry the PAT bearer + the two identity headers; chat completions and models flows work.
2. Live smoke against a Copilot Business seat: `/provider copilot` + pasted fine-grained PAT connects, model list loads, one completion round-trips.
3. OAuth path regression: device-flow token still exchanges, refresh-in-lead behavior preserved (existing tests green).
4. Docs (`docs/` provider page) updated: three supported credentials — device flow (recommended), `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env (OAuth token or fine-grained PAT), classic `ghp_` never supported.

## Notes / honesty
`copilot-developer-cli` is the official CLI's client identity — we present the same first-party integration id the official CLI uses, with the user's own token and seat. GitHub documents fine-grained PATs for the Copilot CLI; using the same identity from a third-party harness is a gray zone users accept knowingly (same pattern as OSS `copilot-api`/`copilot2api` mimicking `vscode-chat`).


## Related UX gap (same card): `/provider export`
There is no fa surface to reveal a stored credential (`/key` is `set|delete` only), so moving the device-flow token to a headless box needs raw `security` incantations. Add one minimal command:

- `/provider export` — copies the full token of the saved Copilot account to the **clipboard**. That's all: no printing to the transcript, no flags, no reveal ceremony. Several accounts → reuse the existing account picker. Feedback is one line: `token copied to clipboard`.

Token-lifetime note (verified): device-flow `gho_`/`ghu_` tokens do not expire and are not refreshed (revocation is manual); only the exchanged ~30-min Copilot API token rotates, which fa re-exchanges automatically — so an exported token stays valid until revoked.

# gh-1606: Copilot provider: support fine-grained PATs directly (skip exchange, send copilot-developer-cli identity headers) — enables COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN in headless

## Description

## Problem
fa's `copilot` provider only supports one auth path: exchange a GitHub credential via `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token`. That endpoint accepts **only OAuth tokens** (`gho_`/`ghu_` from device flow) — a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`) gets **404** on exchange, and direct Copilot API calls with a raw PAT from a generic HTTP client get **400 "Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint"**. So users who provision a fine-grained PAT (the officially documented token type for Copilot automation) cannot use it in fa at all — while the **official GitHub Copilot CLI can**.

## Evidence (verified empirically, 2026-10-14, Copilot Business seat `copilot_for_business_seat_quota`)
- PAT on exchange: `GET https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` → **404** (any headers/UA, incl. h2, exact CLI UA, `client_id` variants).
- PAT direct on `https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/models` with generic client → **400** `Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint`.
- **PAT + first-party client identity → 200 everywhere.** Adding exactly two headers makes the identical request succeed from plain curl:
  ```
  copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli
  user-agent: copilot/1.0.97 (darwin …) term/unknown
  ```
  - `GET  /models`            → 200 (48 models)
  - `POST /chat/completions`  → 200, real completion (claude-fable-5.1 answered)
- MITM of the official Copilot CLI 1.0.95/1.0.97 with `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=<fine-grained PAT>`: it **never calls the exchange** — it sends the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly to `api.business.githubcopilot.com` with those two headers. Endpoint choice: the exchange's `endpoints.api` for OAuth tokens; for a PAT the CLI picks the seat's endpoint (business/enterprise) directly.
- `ghp_` classic PATs remain unsupported by Copilot at all (unchanged).

## Why it matters for fa
- Headless/docker: a PAT is the ideal credential — stable, revocable, scope-limited, no keychain, no interactive device flow in a container. `export COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` currently **fails** in fa; with this fix it works.
- OAuth device-flow tokens stay the recommended default (they work in both paths); this adds the PAT path.

## Proposed fix
In the copilot provider (`lib/src/providers/copilot_oauth.dart` + key resolution):
1. When the credential is a fine-grained PAT (`isFineGrainedGitHubPat`): **skip the exchange entirely**; use the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly against the Copilot API base URL (config `baseUrl` / provider profile — no `endpoints.api` to learn).
2. Attach the first-party client identity on all Copilot API requests in PAT mode:
   - `copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`
   - `user-agent: copilot/<fa-version> (<os>) term/unknown`
   (These headers are harmless for the OAuth path; decide whether to also send them there for consistency.)
3. Keep the existing exchange flow for `gho_`/`ghu_`/device-flow tokens, including its proactive ~30-min token refresh (unchanged).
4. Update the connect-error hints: for `github_pat_` stop suggesting only the "Copilot Requests" permission edit; explain that PAT mode needs fa ≥ this version or the official CLI.

## Acceptance
1. Unit/integration test (mocked http): credential `github_pat_…` → no request to `copilot_internal/v2/token` is made; requests carry the PAT bearer + the two identity headers; chat completions and models flows work.
2. Live smoke against a Copilot Business seat: `/provider copilot` + pasted fine-grained PAT connects, model list loads, one completion round-trips.
3. OAuth path regression: device-flow token still exchanges, refresh-in-lead behavior preserved (existing tests green).
4. Docs (`docs/` provider page) updated: three supported credentials — device flow (recommended), `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env (OAuth token or fine-grained PAT), classic `ghp_` never supported.

## Notes / honesty
`copilot-developer-cli` is the official CLI's client identity — we present the same first-party integration id the official CLI uses, with the user's own token and seat. GitHub documents fine-grained PATs for the Copilot CLI; using the same identity from a third-party harness is a gray zone users accept knowingly (same pattern as OSS `copilot-api`/`copilot2api` mimicking `vscode-chat`).


## Related UX gap (same card): `/provider export`
There is no fa surface to reveal a stored credential (`/key` is `set|delete` only), so moving the device-flow token to a headless box needs raw `security` incantations. Add one minimal command:

- `/provider export` — copies the full token of the saved Copilot account to the **clipboard**. That's all: no printing to the transcript, no flags, no reveal ceremony. Several accounts → reuse the existing account picker. Feedback is one line: `token copied to clipboard`.

Token-lifetime note (verified): device-flow `gho_`/`ghu_` tokens do not expire and are not refreshed (revocation is manual); only the exchanged ~30-min Copilot API token rotates, which fa re-exchanges automatically — so an exported token stays valid until revoked.

This is the only request shape the Copilot API accepts a PAT with; `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` now works headless. - New `/provider export`: copies the saved Copilot account's full token to the clipboard (single account = no ceremony; several = the existing account picker; feedback is one line `token copied to clipboard`; the token never prints to the transcript). - Connect flow updated: the PAT paste hint explains direct-PAT mode (device flow stays recommended); a dead PAT surfaces at the model fetch ("no models for this PAT — check Copilot Requests permission/seat") instead of a forecast exchange 404. ### Key decisions - **PAT mode lives in the token source**: `CopilotTokenManager.get()` short-circuits PATs (no exchange, no cache, no refresh); `copilotRequestHeaders()` dispatches request headers by token shape — an exchanged token keeps the `vscode-chat` identity byte-for-byte, a PAT presents `copilot-developer-cli`.
