# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

Now I understand the problem fully:

`_effectivePlatform(String? platform)` has:
- Complexity 5 (branch points: 4 if statements + the implicit entry)
- Coverage 25% — on the Linux CI runner, the test pins `platform:` explicitly so the `if (platform != null) return platform;` line IS covered (tests with explicit platforms). Wait, let's count: the tests always pass `platform:` explicitly, so only `if (platform != null) return platform;` is covered. The `Platform.isMacOS`, `Platform.isLinux`, `Platform.isWindows` lines are never covered because platform is always non-null in tests. That's 1 of 5 statements → 25%? Hmm, wait: 5 statements:
1. `if (platform != null) return platform;` — covered
2. `if (Platform.isMacOS) return 'macos';` — not covered
3. `if (Platform.isLinux) return 'linux';` — partially (condition evaluated, returns on the CI runner... actually on Linux CI, `Platform.isLinux` is true, so if the function is called with platform==null, this WOULD be covered. But no test calls it with null.)
4. `if (Platform.isWindows) return 'windows';` — not covered
5. `return null;` — not covered

Coverage is 25% = 1/4 lines? The function has 5 lines of code; maybe crap4dart counts statement/line coverage differently. Anyway: cov=25%, comp=5 → CRAP = 25×(1−0.25)³+5 = 25×0.421875+5 = 15.546875 ≈ 15.55. ✓

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

Now I understand the problem fully:

`_effectivePlatform(String? platform)` has:
- Complexity 5 (branch points: 4 if statements + the implicit entry)
- Coverage 25% — on the Linux CI runner, the test pins `platform:` explicitly so the `if (platform != null) return platform;` line IS covered (tests with explicit platforms). Wait, let's count: the tests always pass `platform:` explicitly, so only `if (platform != null) return platform;` is covered. The `Platform.isMacOS`, `Platform.isLinux`, `Platform.isWindows` lines are never covered because platform is always non-null in tests. That's 1 of 5 statements → 25%? Hmm, wait: 5 statements:
1. `if (platform != null) return platform;` — covered
2. `if (Platform.isMacOS) return 'macos';` — not covered
3. `if (Platform.isLinux) return 'linux';` — partially (condition evaluated, returns on the CI runner... actually on Linux CI, `Platform.isLinux` is true, so if the function is called with platform==null, this WOULD be covered. But no test calls it with null.)
4. `if (Platform.isWindows) return 'windows';` — not covered
5. `return null;` — not covered

Coverage is 25% = 1/4 lines? The function has 5 lines of code; maybe crap4dart counts statement/line coverage differently. Anyway: cov=25%, comp=5 → CRAP = 25×(1−0.25)³+5 = 25×0.421875+5 = 15.546875 ≈ 15.55. ✓

How is `_effectivePlatform` invoked without a platform pin? Only via `writeClipboardText` without `platform:` — no test does that. The function is private (`_effectivePlatform`), so it can't be called directly from tests. Hmm.

Wait — how would we increase coverage of a private function? Tests could call `writeClipboardText` without `platform:` — then on the Linux CI runner, `_effectivePlatform(null)` executes: `if (platform != null)` → false (covered again), `Platform.isMacOS` → false, `Platform.isLinux` → true → return 'linux'. That covers lines 2 and 3 — cov becomes 3/5 = 60%: CRAP = 25 × (0.4)³ + 5 = 25 × 0.064 + 5 = 1.6 + 5 = 6.6. 

But wait — can tests call `writeClipboardText` without a platform on macOS/Windows dev machines? On macOS, it'd return 'macos' and try to run pbcopy with the injected runner... the runner is injected, so no real pbcopy runs. On Windows, 'windows' → clip with injected runner. On Linux → 'linux'. So a test like "the default platform resolves through the host Platform and still uses the injected runner" would cover the host-detection lines on ALL dev platforms.

But the `Platform.isWindows` line and `return null` line would still be uncovered on Linux CI:
- On Linux CI: `isMacOS` (false branch), `isLinux` (true) covered. `isWindows` and `return null` never run.
- Coverage = 4/5 = 80% → CRAP = 25 × (0.2)³ + 5 = 25 × 0.008 + 5 = 0.2 + 5 = 5.2. Passes easily.

Hmm, but what does crap4dart measure — line coverage of the file from lcov? The reported cov was 25% (1/4 = 25% or 1.25/5?). Let me think: maybe it counts the 4 branches/lines: lines 54-61 contain: `if (platform != null) return platform;` (line 57), `if (Platform.isMacOS) return 'macos';` (58), `if (Platform.isLinux) return 'linux';` (59), `if (Platform.isWindows) return 'windows';` (60), `return null;` (61). That's 5 executable lines; 1 covered → 20%? The report says 25%. Whatever the exact counting, adding a host-platform test pushes coverage well above 35% (the pass threshold at comp=5).

Alternative approach — reduce complexity to 4:
```dart
String? _effectivePlatform(String? platform) {
  if (platform != null) return platform;
  if (Platform.isMacOS) return 'macos';
  if (Platform.isLinux) return 'linux';
  return Platform.isWindows ? 'windows' : null;
}
```
That's still comp 5 (ternary counts). Not better.

Restructure with a map lookup:
```dart
String? _effectivePlatform(String? platform) {
  if (platform != null) return platform;
  return const {
    'macos': 'macos',
    'linux': 'linux',
    'windows': 'windows',
  }[Platform.operatingSystem];
}
```
comp = 2. CRAP at 0% coverage = 4+2 = 6. Passes regardless of coverage! And it's simpler code.

But wait — the guideline says TDD: "NEVER change production code in response to a review comment or CI failure without a test that first reproduces it". The CI failure here is the CRAP gate. The proper TDD approach for a CRAP fix: write/extend a test that covers the uncovered path (RED = gate fails now; GREEN = after fix, gate passes). The "test that reproduces the issue" for a coverage gate is a test covering the uncovered branch.

Two clean options:
**Option A (test-only)**: Add a test that calls `writeClipboardText` WITHOUT `platform:` (host resolution path) — on the Linux CI runner it covers `isMacOS` (false) + `isLinux` (true) → coverage jumps from 25% to ≥ 60% → CRAP = 6.6 ≤ 12. Production code untouched. This preserves the established "platform pin for tests" seam design.

Wait, but does that fully exercise? On Linux CI: platform=null → `if (platform != null)` false-covered... it already was covered (line 57 was the covered one). Now `isMacOS` false, `isLinux` true return 'linux'. Lines 60 (`isWindows`) and 61 (`return null`) stay uncovered. 3/5 = 60% → CRAP = 25×0.4³+5 = 6.6. ✓ Passes.

**Option B (code simplification + test)**: Replace the if-chain with a `Platform.operatingSystem` map lookup — comp drops to 2, CRAP ≤ 6 even at 0% coverage. More robust against future runner changes (e.g., if the gate ever runs on macOS where isLinux=false, isWindows=false, return null → covered... fine too).

Which is more in line with repo conventions? Let me check how similar platform-detection code is done elsewhere in the codebase. # pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
gates:
  # Issue #1234: the whole-tree ≤2800-line guard (was stage_size +
  # ci.yml shell find-exec, gh-1232). wc -l semantics, generated output
  # excluded — nothing exceeds 2800 today, so the shrink-only baseline
  # starts EMPTY of loc entries. Scope = the package sources [lib, bin]:
  # 0.11.0 has NO per-gate sources override (gates.loc.sources is a
  # ConfigException — caught by CI on 019ede65), and the top-level
  # sources drive the CRAP census too, so they stay untouched. test/ and
  # example/ are enforced by the companion config
  # crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml (same loc gate, sources [test, example]);
  # the app package's own config covers flutter_app/lib.
  loc:
    enabled: true
    max_lines: 2800
    exclude:
      - '**.g.dart'
      - '**.freezed.dart'
      - '**.mocks.dart'
      - 'vendor/**'
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false} # follow-up card (issue #1234 §5). Known
    # FPs to exclude when enabling: the conditional-export IO entry points
    # (lib/io.dart, lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart — public barrels whose
    # importers live outside this repo's import graph) and shared pinned
    # data modules imported only from test/ (lib/src/cli/omp_reg_scenarios.dart,
    # issue #810). lib/fanet.dart was the one confirmed-dead hit — deleted
    # in #1234.
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  # Type-2 duplication gate (issue #1106, crap4dart 0.11.0). Renamed-clone
  # detection on top of the Type-1 default; the union with the raw pass can
  # only ADD findings, never lose exact copies. severity: warning starts
  # soft — escalate to error once the 13-file triage debt is paid
  # (follow-up, owner-side). The global jscpd <1% guards stay as-is.
  #
  # Two suppression channels with different contracts:
  # - `// crap:ignore` (needs ignorable: true) = a JUSTIFIED structural
  #   twin, suppressed forever, with a one-line reason in the comment.
  # - `.crap-baseline.json` (via `check --baseline`) = LEGACY debt; the
  #   committed snapshot must only SHRINK: after each triage batch re-run
  #   `dart pub global run crap4dart check --save-baseline` and commit the
  #   only-down diff, or the snapshot rots and starts masking shifts.
  #
  # WINDOW (until severity flips to error): the gate never fails a build —
  # new (not-baselined) duplication only surfaces as a `[WARN]` line in
  # `check` output. Enforcement becomes hard exactly when the owner-side
  # escalation lands; from then on any finding outside the two channels

  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

blocks.text:
Now I understand the problem fully:

`_effectivePlatform(String? platform)` has:
- Complexity 5 (branch points: 4 if statements + the implicit entry)
- Coverage 25% — on the Linux CI runner, the test pins `platform:` explicitly so the `if (platform != null) return platform;` line IS covered (tests with explicit platforms). Wait, let's count: the tests always pass `platform:` explicitly, so only `if (platform != null) return platform;` is covered. The `Platform.isMacOS`, `Platform.isLinux`, `Platform.isWindows` lines are never covered because platform is always non-null in tests. That's 1 of 5 statements → 25%? Hmm, wait: 5 statements:
1. `if (platform != null) return platform;` — covered
2. `if (Platform.isMacOS) return 'macos';` — not covered
3. `if (Platform.isLinux) return 'linux';` — partially (condition evaluated, returns on the CI runner... actually on Linux CI, `Platform.isLinux` is true, so if the function is called with platform==null, this WOULD be covered. But no test calls it with null.)
4. `if (Platform.isWindows) return 'windows';` — not covered
5. `return null;` — not covered

Coverage is 25% = 1/4 lines? The function has 5 lines of code; maybe crap4dart counts statement/line coverage differently. Anyway: cov=25%, comp=5 → CRAP = 25×(1−0.25)³+5 = 25×0.421875+5 = 15.546875 ≈ 15.55. ✓

How is `_effectivePlatform` invoked without a platform pin? Only via `writeClipboardText` without `platform:` — no test does that. The function is private (`_effectivePlatform`), so it can't be called directly from tests. Hmm.

Wait — how would we increase coverage of a private function? Tests could call `writeClipboardText` without `platform:` — then on the Linux CI runner, `_effectivePlatform(null)` executes: `if (platform != null)` → false (covered again), `Platform.isMacOS` → false, `Platform.isLinux` → true → return 'linux'. That covers lines 2 and 3 — cov becomes 3/5 = 60%: CRAP = 25 × (0.4)³ + 5 = 25 × 0.064 + 5 = 1.6 + 5 = 6.6. 

But wait — can tests call `writeClipboardText` without a platform on macOS/Windows dev machines? On macOS, it'd return 'macos' and try to run pbcopy with the injected runner... the runner is injected, so no real pbcopy runs. On Windows, 'windows' → clip with injected runner. On Linux → 'linux'. So a test like "the default platform resolves through the host Platform and still uses the injected runner" would cover the host-detection lines on ALL dev platforms.

But the `Platform.isWindows` line and `return null` line would still be uncovered on Linux CI:
- On Linux CI: `isMacOS` (false branch), `isLinux` (true) covered. `isWindows` and `return null` never run.
- Coverage = 4/5 = 80% → CRAP = 25 × (0.2)³ + 5 = 25 × 0.008 + 5 = 0.2 + 5 = 5.2. Passes easily.

Hmm, but what does crap4dart measure — line coverage of the file from lcov? The reported cov was 25% (1/4 = 25% or 1.25/5?). Let me think: maybe it counts the 4 branches/lines: lines 54-61 contain: `if (platform != null) return platform;` (line 57), `if (Platform.isMacOS) return 'macos';` (58), `if (Platform.isLinux) return 'linux';` (59), `if (Platform.isWindows) return 'windows';` (60), `return null;` (61). That's 5 executable lines; 1 covered → 20%? The report says 25%. Whatever the exact counting, adding a host-platform test pushes coverage well above 35% (the pass threshold at comp=5).

Alternative approach — reduce complexity to 4:
```dart
String? _effectivePlatform(String? platform) {
  if (platform != null) return platform;
  if (Platform.isMacOS) return 'macos';
  if (Platform.isLinux) return 'linux';
  return Platform.isWindows ? 'windows' : null;
}
```
That's still comp 5 (ternary counts). Not better.

Restructure with a map lookup:
```dart
String? _effectivePlatform(String? platform) {
  if (platform != null) return platform;
  return const {
    'macos': 'macos',
    'linux': 'linux',
    'windows': 'windows',
  }[Platform.operatingSystem];
}
```
comp = 2. CRAP at 0% coverage = 4+2 = 6. Passes regardless of coverage! And it's simpler code.

But wait — the guideline says TDD: "NEVER change production code in response to a review comment or CI failure without a test that first reproduces it". The CI failure here is the CRAP gate. The proper TDD approach for a CRAP fix: write/extend a test that covers the uncovered path (RED = gate fails now; GREEN = after fix, gate passes). The "test that reproduces the issue" for a coverage gate is a test covering the uncovered branch.

Two clean options:
**Option A (test-only)**: Add a test that calls `writeClipboardText` WITHOUT `platform:` (host resolution path) — on the Linux CI runner it covers `isMacOS` (false) + `isLinux` (true) → coverage jumps from 25% to ≥ 60% → CRAP = 6.6 ≤ 12. Production code untouched. This preserves the established "platform pin for tests" seam design.

Wait, but does that fully exercise? On Linux CI: platform=null → `if (platform != null)` false-covered... it already was covered (line 57 was the covered one). Now `isMacOS` false, `isLinux` true return 'linux'. Lines 60 (`isWindows`) and 61 (`return null`) stay uncovered. 3/5 = 60% → CRAP = 25×0.4³+5 = 6.6. ✓ Passes.

**Option B (code simplification + test)**: Replace the if-chain with a `Platform.operatingSystem` map lookup — comp drops to 2, CRAP ≤ 6 even at 0% coverage. More robust against future runner changes (e.g., if the gate ever runs on macOS where isLinux=false, isWindows=false, return null → covered... fine too).

Which is more in line with repo conventions? Let me check how similar platform-detection code is done elsewhere in the codebase. Also, there's `crap4dart.yaml` config with a `max_crap` threshold of 12. Let me also check if there's a baseline file `.crap-baseline.json` — maybe the pattern is to add baselines? Let me look.

  # move — readPasteboardImage 16.32 (split into fake-seam /

  # discoverTaskAgents, _rebuild) split into cohesive sub-dispatchers,
  # the four 0%-cov CC-3 methods covered by tests (frontmatter, video
  # endpoint, below-window ingest, provider picker), the named CC-9 tier
  # split, and _listModels (20 @ 0%) covered by the line-mode /models
  # test. But the FIRST real whole-tree measurement (the authoring box
  # had no dart toolchain) shows the 12.0 → 8.0 repin is not earned yet:
  # 137 methods measure above 8.0 — 54 at exactly 12.00 (the CC-3 @ 0%
  # tier + fully-covered CC-12 dispatchers) and 83 at 9.00 (CC-9 @ 100%).
  # Threshold stays at the measured max; the 12.00/9.00 tier is the next
  # ladder card (cover the CC-3@0% half, split the CC-12 dispatchers,
  # then the threshold follows down to 8.0). Only down from here.
  threshold: 12.0
  # _listModels used to hit 20 with 0% coverage (line-mode-only output);
  # covered by test/cli/provider_models_line_mode_test.dart in #1234.

# ─── loc gate (issue #1234, gh-1232 migration) ─────────────────────────────
# The ≤2800-line file guard MOVED from scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_size +
# the ci.yml shell find-exec guards onto crap4dart's `loc` gate (0.11.0,
# maintainer-confirmed wc -l semantics). Enforced whole-tree on every merge
# validation via `crap4dart check --baseline` (CI quality-gates step) and
# staged files in the pre-commit hook — no staged-scoping escape, no
# hook-dependence, merge-bot merges included. max_lines only DOWN;
# app_localizations.dart is gen-l10n OUTPUT (no .g.dart suffix) — excluded,
# not baselined.

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only broken_goldens is
# enforced here, everything else is disabled explicitly so a bare
# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the
# pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
gates:
  # Issue #1234: the whole-tree ≤2800-line guard (was stage_size +
  # ci.yml shell find-exec, gh-1232). wc -l semantics, generated output
  # excluded — nothing exceeds 2800 today, so the shrink-only baseline
  # starts EMPTY of loc entries. Scope = the package sources [lib, bin]:
  # 0.11.0 has NO per-gate sources override (gates.loc.sources is a
  # ConfigException — caught by CI on 019ede65), and the top-level
  # sources drive the CRAP census too, so they stay untouched. test/ and
  # example/ are enforced by the companion config
  # crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml (same loc gate, sources [test, example]);
  # the app package's own config covers flutter_app/lib.
  loc:
    enabled: true
    max_lines: 2800
    exclude:
      - '**.g.dart'
      - '**.freezed.dart'
      - '**.mocks.dart'
      - 'vendor/**'
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false} # follow-up card (issue #1234 §5). Known
    # FPs to exclude when enabling: the conditional-export IO entry points
    # (lib/io.dart, lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart — public barrels whose
    # importers live outside this repo's import graph) and shared pinned
    # data modules imported only from test/ (lib/src/cli/omp_reg_scenarios.dart,
    # issue #810). lib/fanet.dart was the one confirmed-dead hit — deleted
    # in #1234.
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  # Type-2 duplication gate (issue #1106, crap4dart 0.11.0). Renamed-clone
  # detection on top of the Type-1 default; the union with the raw pass can
  # only ADD findings, never lose exact copies. severity: warning starts
  # soft — escalate to error once the 13-file triage debt is paid
  # (follow-up, owner-side). The global jscpd <1% guards stay as-is.
  #
  # Two suppression channels with different contracts:
  # - `// crap:ignore` (needs ignorable: true) = a JUSTIFIED structural
  #   twin, suppressed forever, with a one-line reason in the comment.
  # - `.crap-baseline.json` (via `check --baseline`) = LEGACY debt; the
  #   committed snapshot must only SHRINK: after each triage batch re-run
  #   `dart pub global run crap4dart check --save-baseline` and commit the
  #   only-down diff, or the snapshot rots and starts masking shifts.
  #
  # WINDOW (until severity flips to error): the gate never fails a build —
  # new (not-baselined) duplication only surfaces as a `[WARN]` line in
  # `check` output. Enforcement becomes hard exactly when the owner-side
  # escalation lands; from then on any finding outside the two channels
  # fails CI/pre-commit.
  duplication:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    ignorable: true # enables `// crap:ignore` for justified structural twins
    ignore_locals: true # Type-2: rename locals before hashing (API names stay)
    ignore_literals: false # keeps l10n/theme/symbol tables out
    sources: # cross-module scope from #487
      - flutter_app/lib
      - packages/fa_ui/lib
      - packages/fa_llm/lib
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}
  golden: {enabled: false} # flutter-only gate (core is not a Flutter project)
  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over core test/ goldens — none exist today, so this is a
  # no-op that guards the future (issue #447 AC: "and core test/ goldens
  # if any appear"). WARNING, same rationale as flutter_app: the 0.9.5
  # detector misses the Ahem-solid-rect and hollow-square classes and
  # false-positives on V-converging shapes; flip to error when the
  # upstream detector fixes land.
  broken_goldens:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    dirs: [test]
    exclude:

      # trips the stripe heuristic (measured 14/14 "overflow stripes" —
      # the same yellow-on-dark detector bug the issue documents for
      # apps_panel/panel_dark). Revisit when upstream fixes land.
      - 'test/integration/**'

Now I understand the setup. The CRAP threshold is 12.0, ratchet: "pushes may only make the codebase BETTER, never worse".

The failing function `_effectivePlatform` in `lib/src/cli/clipboard_writer.dart` is NEW code added by this PR (gh-1606). It has comp=5, cov=25% → CRAP 15.55 > 12.

The fix strategy per repo conventions: the file already documents that the explicit `platform` pin exists because "the macOS/Windows paths are unreachable on a Linux CI runner". The cleanest fix aligned with the TDD approach:

1. RED: add a test that reproduces the low-coverage scenario — call `writeClipboardText` WITHOUT the `platform:` pin (exercising the host-Platform resolution path) with an injected runner. On the Linux CI runner this covers `Platform.isMacOS` (false) and `Platform.isLinux` (true) → coverage rises from 25% to ≥60% → CRAP = 25×0.4³+5 = 6.6.

Wait — but actually there's a subtlety: a test without a platform pin on a macOS dev machine would return 'macos' and call the injected runner once (fine, injected). On Windows dev machine → 'windows' path (fine, injected). All fine because the runner is injected.

But hold on — is a test-only fix "minimum code change"? The TDD rule says: never change production code without a test that reproduces the issue; fix = minimum change. Here the "issue" is untested code → the natural fix is to TEST the code, not rewrite it. Rewriting working, documented code to dodge the metric would also change behavior surface (Platform.operatingSystem vs isX chains are equivalent though).

Actually let me reconsider: is there a way to also cover the windows-return and null-return lines? Not on a Linux runner — `Platform.isWindows` is false there, and `return null` is unreachable via the public API on any of the three real platforms... Actually on Linux: isMacOS false → isLinux true → returns. On macOS: isMacOS true. On Windows: isMacOS false, isLinux false, isWindows true. So `return null` is NEVER reachable via the public API on any desktop platform (the three isX checks cover all Platform.operatingSystem values that... well, not quite — there are other platforms like android, ios, fuchsia! On Android/iOS/Fuchsia, all three are false → return null. But clipboard writing is a CLI/desktop feature; tests run on Linux/macOS/Windows in CI).

So with the test added (no platform pin), coverage on Linux CI: lines covered = `if (platform != null)` (both branches), `isMacOS` check, `isLinux` check+return. Not covered: `isWindows` line, `return null`. That's 3/5 = 60% → CRAP 6.6. ✓

Hmm, but wait: how does crap4dart compute line coverage from lcov? The lcov from dart test gives per-line hit counts. Lines 54-61:
```

59:   if (Platform.isLinux) return 'linux';
60:   if (Platform.isWindows) return 'windows';
61:   return null;

```

Executable lines: 56 (function entry — often not counted separately or counted), 57, 58, 59, 60, 61. The report says cov 25%: if 4 lines counted (57,58,59,60 or 57-61 with... hmm 1/4=25%). Whatever — adding the host-platform test covers 57 (again), 58, 59 → at least 3/5 or 3/4 = 60-75% → CRAP ≤ 25×0.4³+5 = 6.6. Either way well under 12.

Also worth checking: does the merged-shard lcov even include test/cli/clipboard_writer_test.dart? The coverage in CI comes from "test-core → dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage". The new test file `test/cli/clipboard_writer_test.dart` presumably ran in one of the shards — the coverage shows 25% for `_effectivePlatform`, which means yes, the file IS in the coverage and the pinned-platform tests ran. Good — adding another test in the same file will be picked up by the same shard.

Now — per TDD rules, is a test-only change the right fix? The instruction R1: "NEVER change production code in response to a review comment or CI failure without a test that first reproduces it". A test-only fix needs no production change at all. The red state: run crap4dart analyze now → fails (15.55). Green: after adding the test, coverage rises → 6.6.

But hold on — I should also check the OTHER new code in this PR for CRAP proximity. From the CI report:
- `12.00   97.1  N/A   12  _runCopilotStream  lib/src/providers/copilot.dart:81` — exactly at 12.00, passes (>12 fails).

Note the interplay: the tests must cover the *host-platform* branch. But careful: the comment says "the macOS/Windows paths are unreachable on a Linux CI runner" — the whole point of the `platform` pin. A no-pin test on Linux covers only the linux arm. Fine.

However, there's an important consideration: CI also runs on macOS? The "Core tests" shards run on ubuntu-24.04-arm (from the log). And `dart test` locally here runs on Linux too. So the no-pin test on Linux covers isMacOS-false + isLinux-true.

What about `Platform.isWindows` → still 0 coverage on Linux runners, and `return null` → 0. CRAP with 3/5 = 60%: 25×(0.4)³+5 = 6.6. 

Hmm wait, actually let me recompute what crap4dart counts. cov 25% currently. If it counts 4 lines (57,58,59,60) → 1/4 = 25%. Adding the test covers 57 (already), 58, 59 → 3/4 = 75% → CRAP = 25×(0.25)³+5 = 5.39. If it counts 5 lines (57-61) → 1/5 = 20% ≠ 25%. If it counts 57,58,59,60,61 and partially... 1/4 exactly matches 25%, so probably 4 executable lines are tracked (dart's lcov might not emit a record for the `return null` line, or function-entry lines merge). Either way we're comfortably under threshold after the test.

  echo "🧪 Running dart test --coverage (excluding integration tests)..."
  rm -rf coverage
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration
  # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites are
  # integration-tagged — the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
  # lib/src/cli hits from them — so the unit run above skips them. Their
  # hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers (>= 80% ratchet, PR
  # diff-coverage, CRAP: jsr_cli.dart at 0% line coverage reads CRAP 156
  # against the 12.0 ceiling), so the trio runs into the SAME coverage/
  # dir; format_coverage merges the per-isolate files. Keep this list in
  # sync with ci.yml (test-core shard 0); gh-1538 retired the nightly.yml
  # full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the single unit-lcov producer.
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --tags integration \
    test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart \
    test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart \
    test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart \
    --coverage=coverage
}

stage_coverage() {
  if [ ! -d coverage ]; then
    echo "❌ coverage/ not found — run the test-core stage first" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "📊 Formatting coverage to lcov..."
  dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info
  echo "🔍 Checking line coverage (baseline: >= ${COVERAGE_BASELINE}%)..."
  if ! python3 scripts/check_coverage.py "$COVERAGE_BASELINE"; then
    echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — TEST COVERAGE (baseline ${COVERAGE_BASELINE}%)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

Now I understand the problem fully:

`_effectivePlatform(String? platform)` has:
- Complexity 5 (branch points: 4 if statements + the implicit entry)
- Coverage 25% — on the Linux CI runner, the test pins `platform:` explicitly so the `if (platform != null) return platform;` line IS covered (tests with explicit platforms). Wait, let's count: the tests always pass `platform:` explicitly, so only `if (platform != null) return platform;` is covered. The `Platform.isMacOS`, `Platform.isLinux`, `Platform.isWindows` lines are never covered because platform is always non-null in tests. That's 1 of 5 statements → 25%? Hmm, wait: 5 statements:
1. `if (platform != null) return platform;` — covered
2. `if (Platform.isMacOS) return 'macos';` — not covered
3. `if (Platform.isLinux) return 'linux';` — partially (condition evaluated, returns on the CI runner... actually on Linux CI, `Platform.isLinux` is true, so if the function is called with platform==null, this WOULD be covered. But no test calls it with null.)
4. `if (Platform.isWindows) return 'windows';` — not covered
5. `return null;` — not covered

Coverage is 25% = 1/4 lines? The function has 5 lines of code; maybe crap4dart counts statement/line coverage differently. Anyway: cov=25%, comp=5 → CRAP = 25×(1−0.25)³+5 = 25×0.421875+5 = 15.546875 ≈ 15.55. ✓

How is `_effectivePlatform` invoked without a platform pin? Only via `writeClipboardText` without `platform:` — no test does that. The function is private (`_effectivePlatform`), so it can't be called directly from tests. Hmm.

Wait — how would we increase coverage of a private function? Tests could call `writeClipboardText` without `platform:` — then on the Linux CI runner, `_effectivePlatform(null)` executes: `if (platform != null)` → false (covered again), `Platform.isMacOS` → false, `Platform.isLinux` → true → return 'linux'. That covers lines 2 and 3 — cov becomes 3/5 = 60%: CRAP = 25 × (0.4)³ + 5 = 25 × 0.064 + 5 = 1.6 + 5 = 6.6. 

But wait — can tests call `writeClipboardText` without a platform on macOS/Windows dev machines? On macOS, it'd return 'macos' and try to run pbcopy with the injected runner... the runner is injected, so no real pbcopy runs. On Windows, 'windows' → clip with injected runner. On Linux → 'linux'. So a test like "the default platform resolves through the host Platform and still uses the injected runner" would cover the host-detection lines on ALL dev platforms.

But the `Platform.isWindows` line and `return null` line would still be uncovered on Linux CI:
- On Linux CI: `isMacOS` (false branch), `isLinux` (true) covered. `isWindows` and `return null` never run.
- Coverage = 4/5 = 80% → CRAP = 25 × (0.2)³ + 5 = 25 × 0.008 + 5 = 0.2 + 5 = 5.2. Passes easily.

Hmm, but what does crap4dart measure — line coverage of the file from lcov? The reported cov was 25% (1/4 = 25% or 1.25/5?). Let me think: maybe it counts the 4 branches/lines: lines 54-61 contain: `if (platform != null) return platform;` (line 57), `if (Platform.isMacOS) return 'macos';` (58), `if (Platform.isLinux) return 'linux';` (59), `if (Platform.isWindows) return 'windows';` (60), `return null;` (61). That's 5 executable lines; 1 covered → 20%? The report says 25%. Whatever the exact counting, adding a host-platform test pushes coverage well above 35% (the pass threshold at comp=5).

Alternative approach — reduce complexity to 4:
```dart
String? _effectivePlatform(String? platform) {
  if (platform != null) return platform;
  if (Platform.isMacOS) return 'macos';
  if (Platform.isLinux) return 'linux';
  return Platform.isWindows ? 'windows' : null;
}
```
That's still comp 5 (ternary counts). Not better.

Restructure with a map lookup:
```dart
String? _effectivePlatform(String? platform) {
  if (platform != null) return platform;
  return const {
    'macos': 'macos',
    'linux': 'linux',
    'windows': 'windows',
  }[Platform.operatingSystem];
}
```
comp = 2. CRAP at 0% coverage = 4+2 = 6. Passes regardless of coverage! And it's simpler code.

But wait — the guideline says TDD: "NEVER change production code in response to a review comment or CI failure without a test that first reproduces it". The CI failure here is the CRAP gate. The proper TDD approach for a CRAP fix: write/extend a test that covers the uncovered path (RED = gate fails now; GREEN = after fix, gate passes). The "test that reproduces the issue" for a coverage gate is a test covering the uncovered branch.

Two clean options:
**Option A (test-only)**: Add a test that calls `writeClipboardText` WITHOUT `platform:` (host resolution path) — on the Linux CI runner it covers `isMacOS` (false) + `isLinux` (true) → coverage jumps from 25% to ≥ 60% → CRAP = 6.6 ≤ 12. Production code untouched. This preserves the established "platform pin for tests" seam design.

Wait, but does that fully exercise? On Linux CI: platform=null → `if (platform != null)` false-covered... it already was covered (line 57 was the covered one). Now `isMacOS` false, `isLinux` true return 'linux'. Lines 60 (`isWindows`) and 61 (`return null`) stay uncovered. 3/5 = 60% → CRAP = 25×0.4³+5 = 6.6. ✓ Passes.

**Option B (code simplification + test)**: Replace the if-chain with a `Platform.operatingSystem` map lookup — comp drops to 2, CRAP ≤ 6 even at 0% coverage. More robust against future runner changes (e.g., if the gate ever runs on macOS where isLinux=false, isWindows=false, return null → covered... fine too).

  # ladder card (cover the CC-3@0% half, split the CC-12 dispatchers,
  # then the threshold follows down to 8.0). Only down from here.
  threshold: 12.0
  # _listModels used to hit 20 with 0% coverage (line-mode-only output);
  # covered by test/cli/provider_models_line_mode_test.dart in #1234.

# ─── loc gate (issue #1234, gh-1232 migration) ─────────────────────────────
# The ≤2800-line file guard MOVED from scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_size +
# the ci.yml shell find-exec guards onto crap4dart's `loc` gate (0.11.0,
# maintainer-confirmed wc -l semantics). Enforced whole-tree on every merge
# validation via `crap4dart check --baseline` (CI quality-gates step) and
# staged files in the pre-commit hook — no staged-scoping escape, no
# hook-dependence, merge-bot merges included. max_lines only DOWN;
# app_localizations.dart is gen-l10n OUTPUT (no .g.dart suffix) — excluded,
# not baselined.

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only broken_goldens is
# enforced here, everything else is disabled explicitly so a bare
# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the
# pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
gates:
  # Issue #1234: the whole-tree ≤2800-line guard (was stage_size +
  # ci.yml shell find-exec, gh-1232). wc -l semantics, generated output
  # excluded — nothing exceeds 2800 today, so the shrink-only baseline
  # starts EMPTY of loc entries. Scope = the package sources [lib, bin]:
  # 0.11.0 has NO per-gate sources override (gates.loc.sources is a
  # ConfigException — caught by CI on 019ede65), and the top-level
  # sources drive the CRAP census too, so they stay untouched. test/ and
  # example/ are enforced by the companion config
  # crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml (same loc gate, sources [test, example]);
  # the app package's own config covers flutter_app/lib.
  loc:
    enabled: true
    max_lines: 2800
    exclude:
      - '**.g.dart'
      - '**.freezed.dart'
      - '**.mocks.dart'
      - 'vendor/**'
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false} # follow-up card (issue #1234 §5). Known
    # FPs to exclude when enabling: the conditional-export IO entry points
    # (lib/io.dart, lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart — public barrels whose
    # importers live outside this repo's import graph) and shared pinned
    # data modules imported only from test/ (lib/src/cli/omp_reg_scenarios.dart,
    # issue #810). lib/fanet.dart was the one confirmed-dead hit — deleted
    # in #1234.
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  # Type-2 duplication gate (issue #1106, crap4dart 0.11.0). Renamed-clone
  # detection on top of the Type-1 default; the union with the raw pass can
  # only ADD findings, never lose exact copies. severity: warning starts
  # soft — escalate to error once the 13-file triage debt is paid
  # (follow-up, owner-side). The global jscpd <1% guards stay as-is.
  #
  # Two suppression channels with different contracts:
  # - `// crap:ignore` (needs ignorable: true) = a JUSTIFIED structural
  #   twin, suppressed forever, with a one-line reason in the comment.
  # - `.crap-baseline.json` (via `check --baseline`) = LEGACY debt; the
  #   committed snapshot must only SHRINK: after each triage batch re-run
  #   `dart pub global run crap4dart check --save-baseline` and commit the
  #   only-down diff, or the snapshot rots and starts masking shifts.
  #
  # WINDOW (until severity flips to error): the gate never fails a build —
  # new (not-baselined) duplication only surfaces as a `[WARN]` line in
  # `check` output. Enforcement becomes hard exactly when the owner-side
  # escalation lands; from then on any finding outside the two channels
  # fails CI/pre-commit.

    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    ignorable: true # enables `// crap:ignore` for justified structural twins
    ignore_locals: true # Type-2: rename locals before hashing (API names stay)
    ignore_literals: false # keeps l10n/theme/symbol tables out
    sources: # cross-module scope from #487

      - packages/fa_ui/lib
      - packages/fa_llm/lib

  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}
  golden: {enabled: false} # flutter-only gate (core is not a Flutter project)
  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}

  broken_goldens:

    severity: warning
    dirs: [test]
    exclude:

      # apps_panel/panel_dark). Revisit when upstream fixes land.
      - 'test/integration/**'

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
